+# Backlog
+
+**Staged from:** `.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`, `documentation/PLAN.md`, `deep-research-report.md`
+
+---
+
+## Phase M1 — Research & Backend Selection (Weeks 1–2)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 1.1 | Set up Python environment with MMPose, RTMPose, RTMO                                     | Official install from OpenMMLab docs                     |
+| 1.2 | Benchmark RTMPose-m vs RTMO on target hardware (CPU/GPU)                                | RTMO not yet evaluated per PLAN_SUMMARY                    |
+| 1.3 | ONNX export validation for chosen model                                                    | Required for future optimization (Phase 5)                |
+
+## Phase M2 — External Tracking Runner (Weeks 1–2, overlap)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 2.1 | Build MMPose worker (standalone Python script, CLI entrypoint)                          | Out-of-process by design per PLAN_SUMMARY                  |
+| 2.2 | Implement video-to-JSON inference pipeline                                                | MMPose inferencer → cached JSON outputs                   |
+| 2.3 | Establish tracking result schema                                                           | Must encode 2D keypoints + track IDs per person           |
+
+## Phase M3 — Blender Add-on Skeleton (Weeks 2–3)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 3.1 | Create Blender add-on panel (video input, person selection, output mode)                 | Follows Blender developer conventions                      |
+| 3.2 | Implement subprocess launcher (Blender Python → MMPose worker)                           | JSON-first communication via cached files                 |
+| 3.3 | Implement JSON import from worker output                                                  | Frame-to-frame data exchange                              |
+
+## Phase M4 — Visualization in Blender (Week 3)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 4.1 | Map MMPose keypoints to Blender empties at joint positions                                | 17 COCO body joints per person                            |
+| 4.2 | Add track ID visualization in Blender viewport                                            | Persistent IDs across frames                              |
+| 4.3 | Implement basic temporal smoothing on empty positions between frames                      | Gap fill + interpolation                                  |
+
+## Phase M5 — Retargeting & Animation Mapping (Weeks 5–8)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 5.1 | Skeleton bone mapping (MMPose 17 joints → Blender armature)                              | Rigify, Humanoid, Mixamo presets                          |
+| 5.2 | Automatic armature generation from pose tracks                                            | Phase 2 deliverable                                       |
+| 5.3 | IK/FK retargeting options                                                                | User-selectable                                           |
+| 5.4 | Animation curve generation from pose keyframes                                            | Populated from tracked motion                             |
+| 5.5 | Gap-filling for occluded frames                                                          | Interpolation or ML fill (50+ frame occlusions)           |
+
+## Phase M6 — Multi-Person + Object Tracking (Weeks 9–12)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 6.1 | Integrate SAM 2 for promptable object masks                                                | Phase 3 deliverable                                       |
+| 6.2 | Integrate ByteTrack for general MOT                                                       | Non-human objects in crowded scenes                       |
+| 6.3 | SAM 2 + MMPose composite pipeline                                                         | SAM finds person → MMPose tracks pose                     |
+| 6.4 | Object mask overlays in Blender (compositing/roto)                                       |                                                         |
+
+## Phase M7 — UI Workflow (Weeks 3–8, iterative)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 7.1 | Retarget mode selector + bone mapping config UI                                           |                                                         |
+| 7.2 | Tooltips, presets, keyboard shortcuts                                                    | Phase 5 polish                                            |
+| 7.3 | User workflow testing on diverse rigs                                                      |                                                         |
+
+## Phase M8 — 3D Pose Lifting (Weeks 13–15, if licensing permits)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 8.1 | SMPL / WHAM licensing compliance check                                                    | Major blocker                                             |
+| 8.2 | Optional 2D→3D pose lift from MMPose keypoints                                            | WHAM or alternative                                       |
+| 8.3 | Camera-relative → world-space transform                                                   |                                                         |
+| 8.4 | Fallback to 2D-only when 3D fails                                                         |                                                         |
+
+## Phase M9 — Optimization & Polish (Weeks 16–18)
+
+| #  | Item                                                                                     | Notes                                                    |
+|----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
+| 9.1 | End-to-end profiling (Blender → MMPose → Blender)                                        |                                                         |
+| 9.2 | ONNX export of RTMPose                                                                    | Faster inference                                          |
+| 9.3 | TensorRT backend for GPU optimization                                                     |                                                         |
+| 9.4 | Testing 50+ diverse video sequences                                                       |                                                         |
+| 9.5 | Documentation, tutorials, demo reel                                                       |                                                         |
+
+---
+
+## Dependencies & Blockers
+
+- Phase M6 (SAM 2, ByteTrack) depends on Phase M5 stabilizing first.
+- Phase M8 (3D lifting) is blocked until SMPL licensing is resolved.
+- Hardware requirements are undefined — no target GPU/CPU specification in source plans.
+- Blender version target is unspecified — add-on API compatibility is an open decision.

+# Architecture Decision Log
+
+**Source-plan context:** `.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`, `documentation/PLAN.md`, `deep-research-report.md`
+
+---
+
+## ADR-1: Out-of-Process Inference
+
+**Decision:** All ML inference (MMPose, SAM 2, ByteTrack, WHAM) runs as separate Python subprocesses outside Blender's embedded Python.
+
+**Rationale:** Blender ships its own Python distribution. Embedding PyTorch/CUDA inside Blender's environment is complex and fragile. A separate process avoids DLL conflicts, simplifies dependency management, and lets Blender remain stable even if the inference worker crashes.
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Communication must use IPC (cached JSON files are the default).
+- The MMPose worker requires its own Python environment with PyTorch installed.
+- Slightly higher latency for large data transfer, justified by the decoupling benefit.
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — mandated by all three planning sources.
+
+---
+
+## ADR-2: JSON-First Communication
+
+**Decision:** Data exchange between the MMPose worker and Blender uses cached JSON files, not in-memory pipes or shared libraries.
+
+**Rationale:** JSON files provide a durable, inspectable, and debuggable exchange format. They decouple the inference pipeline from the Blender UI thread. This enables offline processing and re-running steps without re-tracking raw video.
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Requires a defined tracking result schema (BACKLOG item 2.3).
+- File I/O becomes a performance factor — profiled in Phase 9.
+- Parallel workers require unique file paths or lock mechanisms.
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — mandated by all three planning sources.
+
+---
+
+## ADR-3: MMPose/RTMPose as Primary Backend
+
+**Decision:** MMPose (RTMPose family) is the primary pose estimation backend. SAM 2 and ByteTrack are phase-two additions. LoRATv2 is deprecated for v1.
+
+**Rationale:** LoRATv2 outputs bounding boxes, not pose keypoints. Blender users need skeleton tracking for animation, camera rigging, and retargeting. MMPose provides 17 standard COCO keypoints per person with real-time performance (90+ FPS CPU, 430+ FPS GPU).
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Only 17 body joints are tracked in v1 — spine/neck/jaw/finger bones are interpolated.
+- SAM 2/ByteTrack integration is deferred to phase M6.
+- LoRATv2 may be retained as a camera-solving fallback (bounding boxes for tracking reference).
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — resolution documented in PLAN_SUMMARY contradiction section.
+
+---
+
+## ADR-4: Empties as v1 Output
+
+**Decision:** Phase 1 output is Blender empties at keypoint positions. Armature retargeting is deferred to phase M5.
+
+**Rationale:** The source plan explicitly lists armature retargeting as Phase 2 (weeks 5–8). Starting with empties provides immediate value (motion paths, visualization) without the complexity of skeleton mapping.
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Users get pose tracks → empties with motion paths in v1.
+- Full animation pipeline requires Phase 2 delivery.
+- The choice of empty vs. armature for v1 is intentional ambiguity (see Unresolved Decisions below).
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — aligns with phased plan in documentation/PLAN.md.
+
+---
+
+## Unresolved Decisions
+
+### RTMPose-m vs. RTMO for v1
+RTMPose-m has higher COCO AP (75.8); RTMO is faster for multi-person. The source plans do not resolve this. Recommendation: try both during M1 benchmarking (backlog item 1.2).
+
+### Blender version target
+No Blender version is specified in any source plan. Add-on API compatibility (e.g., `bpy.types.Panel` changes between 3.x and 4.x) is a decision that must be made.
+
+### Hardware requirements
+No GPU/CPU requirements are defined. GPU inference needs CUDA-capable hardware; CPU-only targets need RTMPose quantization strategy.
+
+### Distribution model
+Open-source marketplace add-on vs. paid release is undefined. No source plan addresses this.
+
+### SMPL licensing path
+WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration. It is unclear whether a legal/compliance path exists. If blocked, WHAM should be replaced with an alternative (e.g., VideoPose3D).

+# Project Brief — Blender Motion Tracking Enhancement
+
+---
+
+## Purpose
+
+Integrate state-of-the-art human pose tracking into Blender's Video Editor for automatic camera rigging, motion retargeting, and animation. The system takes video input, produces 2D pose tracks with persistent IDs, maps them to Blender empties or armature bones, and optionally lifts to 3D.
+
+## Planning Sources
+
+The project scope is defined by three planning documents:
+
+- **`.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`** — Technical planning summary derived from the master plan and deep research report.
+- **`documentation/PLAN.md`** — 18-week phased implementation plan with milestones and phases.
+- **`deep-research-report.md`** — Comparative analysis of candidate tracking backends (MMPose, SAM 2, ByteTrack, LoRATv2, WHAM).
+
+---
+
+## Recommended Architecture
+
+```
+Video / Still Images
+    → Blender Add-on Panel (launch MMPose worker, configure options)
+        → MMPose Worker (external Python subprocess, RTMPose inference)
+            → 2D Keypoints + Track IDs (cached JSON)
+                → Temporal Smoothing + Gap Fill
+                    → Blender Empties / Armature Bones
+                        → Optional 3D Pose Lift (WHAM, phase-dependent)
+                            → Animation Curves in Scene
+```
+
+## Primary Backend: MMPose / RTMPose
+
+MMPose with RTMPose is the recommended v1 backend. It produces 2D keypoints directly mappable to Blender bones and empties, with real-time performance (90+ FPS on CPU, 430+ FPS on GPU) and an Apache-2.0 license.
+
+## Target Phases
+
+1. **MMPose Integration** (Weeks 1–4): Video → MMPose → empties with keypoints + track IDs.
+2. **Armature Retargeting** (Weeks 5–8): Skeleton bone mapping, automatic armature generation, animation curves.
+3. **Multi-Person + Object Tracking** (Weeks 9–12): SAM 2, ByteTrack, RTMO integration.
+4. **3D Pose Lifting** (Weeks 13–15): Optional 2D→3D lift via WHAM.
+5. **Optimization & Polish** (Weeks 16–18): Latency optimization, TensorRT, UI polish, documentation.
+
+## Why Heavy ML Inference Runs Outside Blender (v1)
+
+Blender ships its own bundled Python distribution. Embedding PyTorch and CUDA inside Blender's Python environment introduces significant complexity:
+
+- **Dependency conflicts:** Blender's Python has its own version and bundled packages. Adding PyTorch (1200+ MB) and CUDA toolkits risks DLL conflicts.
+- **Stability:** A crash in the ML worker would take Blender down with it if embedded. Out-of-process keeps Blender stable.
+- **Distribution:** Shipping a combined Blender + PyTorch installer is impractical — PyTorch alone is 1.2+ GB with CUDA dependencies.
+- **Flexibility:** A separate worker lets users upgrade PyTorch independently, supports GPU/CPU toggle, and enables headless operation on a remote machine.
+
+The out-of-process design is mandated by all three planning sources.
+
+## Why Blender Consumes Cached Tracking Outputs
+
+Communication between Blender and the MMPose worker uses cached JSON files — not in-memory pipes or embedded libraries — because:
+
+- **Inspection & debugging:** JSON files are human-readable. Users can inspect tracking results, compare frames, and debug ID switches without rerunning inference.
+- **Idempotency:** Tracking outputs can be cached and reused. Users can tweak visualization, retargeting, or smoothing without re-tracking video.
+- **Decoupling:** The worker and Blender can run independently. The worker can process multiple videos; Blender can import any cached result at any time.
+- **Simplicity:** File-based exchange avoids complex IPC protocols, shared memory, or network sockets.
+
+## Key Constraints
+
+1. **Not a Python project** — deliverable is a Blender add-on, not a standalone Python repo.
+2. **Monocular 3D ambiguity** — 3D pose lifting is optional; depth recovery from a single camera is inherently ambiguous.
+3. **Identity consistency** — crowded scenes require robust MOT (phase M6) to prevent ID swaps.
+4. **17-joint limitation** — COCO keypoints don't cover spine/neck/jaw/fingers; interpolation is required for full rigs.
+5. **SMPL licensing** — WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration, which is a compliance blocker for Phase 4.
+
+## Scope Boundaries (Out of Scope)
+
+- Writing production code (planning only).
+- Creating Blender files (.blend).
+- Installing ML libraries or setting up environments.
+- 3D character generation, facial expression tracking, hand pose tracking, or live camera capture (future extensions).
+
+## Blockers for Execution
+
+1. **Blender version target** — undefined; add-on API compatibility varies across 3.x/4.x.
+2. **Hardware requirements** — no GPU/CPU specification defined.
+3. **Distribution model** — open-source vs. paid release is undecided.
+4. **RTMPose-m vs. RTMO** — not resolved for v1 primary model selection.
+5. **SMPL licensing path** — WHAM integration depends on legal/compliance clearance.

+# Architecture Decision Log
+
+**Source-plan context:** `.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`, `documentation/PLAN.md`, `deep-research-report.md`
+
+---
+
+## ADR-1: Out-of-Process Inference
+
+**Decision:** All ML inference (MMPose, SAM 2, ByteTrack, WHAM) runs as separate Python subprocesses outside Blender's embedded Python.
+
+**Rationale:** Blender ships its own Python distribution. Embedding PyTorch/CUDA inside Blender's environment is complex and fragile. A separate process avoids DLL conflicts, simplifies dependency management, and lets Blender remain stable even if the inference worker crashes.
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Communication must use IPC (cached JSON files are the default).
+- The MMPose worker requires its own Python environment with PyTorch installed.
+- Slightly higher latency for large data transfer, justified by the decoupling benefit.
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — mandated by all three planning sources.
+
+---
+
+## ADR-2: JSON-First Communication
+
+**Decision:** Data exchange between the MMPose worker and Blender uses cached JSON files, not in-memory pipes or shared libraries.
+
+**Rationale:** JSON files provide a durable, inspectable, and debuggable exchange format. They decouple the inference pipeline from the Blender UI thread. This enables offline processing and re-running steps without re-tracking raw video.
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Requires a defined tracking result schema (BACKLOG item 2.3).
+- File I/O becomes a performance factor — profiled in Phase 9.
+- Parallel workers require unique file paths or lock mechanisms.
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — mandated by all three planning sources.
+
+---
+
+## ADR-3: MMPose/RTMPose as Primary Backend
+
+**Decision:** MMPose (RTMPose family) is the primary pose estimation backend. SAM 2 and ByteTrack are phase-two additions. LoRATv2 is deprecated for v1.
+
+**Rationale:** LoRATv2 outputs bounding boxes, not pose keypoints. Blender users need skeleton tracking for animation, camera rigging, and retargeting. MMPose provides 17 standard COCO keypoints per person with real-time performance (90+ FPS CPU, 430+ FPS GPU).
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Only 17 body joints are tracked in v1 — spine/neck/jaw/finger bones are interpolated.
+- SAM 2/ByteTrack integration is deferred to phase M6.
+- LoRATv2 may be retained as a camera-solving fallback (bounding boxes for tracking reference).
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — resolution documented in PLAN_SUMMARY contradiction section.
+
+---
+
+## ADR-4: Empties as v1 Output
+
+**Decision:** Phase 1 output is Blender empties at keypoint positions. Armature retargeting is deferred to phase M5.
+
+**Rationale:** The source plan explicitly lists armature retargeting as Phase 2 (weeks 5–8). Starting with empties provides immediate value (motion paths, visualization) without the complexity of skeleton mapping.
+
+**Consequences:**
+- Users get pose tracks → empties with motion paths in v1.
+- Full animation pipeline requires Phase 2 delivery.
+- The choice of empty vs. armature for v1 is intentional ambiguity (see Unresolved Decisions below).
+
+**Status:** **Accepted** — aligns with phased plan in documentation/PLAN.md.
+
+---
+
+## Unresolved Decisions
+
+### RTMPose-m vs. RTMO for v1
+RTMPose-m has higher COCO AP (75.8); RTMO is faster for multi-person. The source plans do not resolve this. Recommendation: try both during M1 benchmarking (backlog item 1.2).
+
+### Blender version target
+No Blender version is specified in any source plan. Add-on API compatibility (e.g., `bpy.types.Panel` changes between 3.x and 4.x) is a decision that must be made.
+
+### Hardware requirements
+No GPU/CPU requirements are defined. GPU inference needs CUDA-capable hardware; CPU-only targets need RTMPose quantization strategy.
+
+### Distribution model
+Open-source marketplace add-on vs. paid release is undefined. No source plan addresses this.
+
+### SMPL licensing path
+WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration. It is unclear whether a legal/compliance path exists. If blocked, WHAM should be replaced with an alternative (e.g., VideoPose3D).

+# Project Brief — Blender Motion Tracking Enhancement
+
+---
+
+## Purpose
+
+Integrate state-of-the-art human pose tracking into Blender's Video Editor for automatic camera rigging, motion retargeting, and animation. The system takes video input, produces 2D pose tracks with persistent IDs, maps them to Blender empties or armature bones, and optionally lifts to 3D.
+
+## Planning Sources
+
+The project scope is defined by three planning documents:
+
+- **`.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`** — Technical planning summary derived from the master plan and deep research report.
+- **`documentation/PLAN.md`** — 18-week phased implementation plan with milestones and phases.
+- **`deep-research-report.md`** — Comparative analysis of candidate tracking backends (MMPose, SAM 2, ByteTrack, LoRATv2, WHAM).
+
+---
+
+## Recommended Architecture
+
+```
+Video / Still Images
+    → Blender Add-on Panel (launch MMPose worker, configure options)
+        → MMPose Worker (external Python subprocess, RTMPose inference)
+            → 2D Keypoints + Track IDs (cached JSON)
+                → Temporal Smoothing + Gap Fill
+                    → Blender Empties / Armature Bones
+                        → Optional 3D Pose Lift (WHAM, phase-dependent)
+                            → Animation Curves in Scene
+```
+
+## Primary Backend: MMPose / RTMPose
+
+MMPose with RTMPose is the recommended v1 backend. It produces 2D keypoints directly mappable to Blender bones and empties, with real-time performance (90+ FPS on CPU, 430+ FPS on GPU) and an Apache-2.0 license.
+
+## Target Phases
+
+1. **MMPose Integration** (Weeks 1–4): Video → MMPose → empties with keypoints + track IDs.
+2. **Armature Retargeting** (Weeks 5–8): Skeleton bone mapping, automatic armature generation, animation curves.
+3. **Multi-Person + Object Tracking** (Weeks 9–12): SAM 2, ByteTrack, RTMO integration.
+4. **3D Pose Lifting** (Weeks 13–15): Optional 2D→3D lift via WHAM.
+5. **Optimization & Polish** (Weeks 16–18): Latency optimization, TensorRT, UI polish, documentation.
+
+## Why Heavy ML Inference Runs Outside Blender (v1)
+
+Blender ships its own bundled Python distribution. Embedding PyTorch and CUDA inside Blender's Python environment introduces significant complexity:
+
+- **Dependency conflicts:** Blender's Python has its own version and bundled packages. Adding PyTorch (1200+ MB) and CUDA toolkits risks DLL conflicts.
+- **Stability:** A crash in the ML worker would take Blender down with it if embedded. Out-of-process keeps Blender stable.
+- **Distribution:** Shipping a combined Blender + PyTorch installer is impractical — PyTorch alone is 1.2+ GB with CUDA dependencies.
+- **Flexibility:** A separate worker lets users upgrade PyTorch independently, supports GPU/CPU toggle, and enables headless operation on a remote machine.
+
+The out-of-process design is mandated by all three planning sources.
+
+## Why Blender Consumes Cached Tracking Outputs
+
+Communication between Blender and the MMPose worker uses cached JSON files — not in-memory pipes or embedded libraries — because:
+
+- **Inspection & debugging:** JSON files are human-readable. Users can inspect tracking results, compare frames, and debug ID switches without rerunning inference.
+- **Idempotency:** Tracking outputs can be cached and reused. Users can tweak visualization, retargeting, or smoothing without re-tracking video.
+- **Decoupling:** The worker and Blender can run independently. The worker can process multiple videos; Blender can import any cached result at any time.
+- **Simplicity:** File-based exchange avoids complex IPC protocols, shared memory, or network sockets.
+
+## Key Constraints
+
+1. **Not a Python project** — deliverable is a Blender add-on, not a standalone Python repo.
+2. **Monocular 3D ambiguity** — 3D pose lifting is optional; depth recovery from a single camera is inherently ambiguous.
+3. **Identity consistency** — crowded scenes require robust MOT (phase M6) to prevent ID swaps.
+4. **17-joint limitation** — COCO keypoints don't cover spine/neck/jaw/fingers; interpolation is required for full rigs.
+5. **SMPL licensing** — WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration, which is a compliance blocker for Phase 4.
+
+## Scope Boundaries (Out of Scope)
+
+- Writing production code (planning only).
+- Creating Blender files (.blend).
+- Installing ML libraries or setting up environments.
+- 3D character generation, facial expression tracking, hand pose tracking, or live camera capture (future extensions).
+
+## Blockers for Execution
+
+1. **Blender version target** — undefined; add-on API compatibility varies across 3.x/4.x.
+2. **Hardware requirements** — no GPU/CPU specification defined.
+3. **Distribution model** — open-source vs. paid release is undecided.
+4. **RTMPose-m vs. RTMO** — not resolved for v1 primary model selection.
+5. **SMPL licensing path** — WHAM integration depends on legal/compliance clearance.

+    "patch": "Index: .pm/DECISIONS.md\n===================================================================\n--- .pm/DECISIONS.md\t\n+++ .pm/DECISIONS.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@\n+# Architecture Decision Log\n+\n+**Source-plan context:** `.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`, `documentation/PLAN.md`, `deep-research-report.md`\n+\n+---\n+\n+## ADR-1: Out-of-Process Inference\n+\n+**Decision:** All ML inference (MMPose, SAM 2, ByteTrack, WHAM) runs as separate Python subprocesses outside Blender's embedded Python.\n+\n+**Rationale:** Blender ships its own Python distribution. Embedding PyTorch/CUDA inside Blender's environment is complex and fragile. A separate process avoids DLL conflicts, simplifies dependency management, and lets Blender remain stable even if the inference worker crashes.\n+\n+**Consequences:**\n+- Communication must use IPC (cached JSON files are the default).\n+- The MMPose worker requires its own Python environment with PyTorch installed.\n+- Slightly higher latency for large data transfer, justified by the decoupling benefit.\n+\n+**Status:** **Accepted** — mandated by all three planning sources.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## ADR-2: JSON-First Communication\n+\n+**Decision:** Data exchange between the MMPose worker and Blender uses cached JSON files, not in-memory pipes or shared libraries.\n+\n+**Rationale:** JSON files provide a durable, inspectable, and debuggable exchange format. They decouple the inference pipeline from the Blender UI thread. This enables offline processing and re-running steps without re-tracking raw video.\n+\n+**Consequences:**\n+- Requires a defined tracking result schema (BACKLOG item 2.3).\n+- File I/O becomes a performance factor — profiled in Phase 9.\n+- Parallel workers require unique file paths or lock mechanisms.\n+\n+**Status:** **Accepted** — mandated by all three planning sources.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## ADR-3: MMPose/RTMPose as Primary Backend\n+\n+**Decision:** MMPose (RTMPose family) is the primary pose estimation backend. SAM 2 and ByteTrack are phase-two additions. LoRATv2 is deprecated for v1.\n+\n+**Rationale:** LoRATv2 outputs bounding boxes, not pose keypoints. Blender users need skeleton tracking for animation, camera rigging, and retargeting. MMPose provides 17 standard COCO keypoints per person with real-time performance (90+ FPS CPU, 430+ FPS GPU).\n+\n+**Consequences:**\n+- Only 17 body joints are tracked in v1 — spine/neck/jaw/finger bones are interpolated.\n+- SAM 2/ByteTrack integration is deferred to phase M6.\n+- LoRATv2 may be retained as a camera-solving fallback (bounding boxes for tracking reference).\n+\n+**Status:** **Accepted** — resolution documented in PLAN_SUMMARY contradiction section.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## ADR-4: Empties as v1 Output\n+\n+**Decision:** Phase 1 output is Blender empties at keypoint positions. Armature retargeting is deferred to phase M5.\n+\n+**Rationale:** The source plan explicitly lists armature retargeting as Phase 2 (weeks 5–8). Starting with empties provides immediate value (motion paths, visualization) without the complexity of skeleton mapping.\n+\n+**Consequences:**\n+- Users get pose tracks → empties with motion paths in v1.\n+- Full animation pipeline requires Phase 2 delivery.\n+- The choice of empty vs. armature for v1 is intentional ambiguity (see Unresolved Decisions below).\n+\n+**Status:** **Accepted** — aligns with phased plan in documentation/PLAN.md.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Unresolved Decisions\n+\n+### RTMPose-m vs. RTMO for v1\n+RTMPose-m has higher COCO AP (75.8); RTMO is faster for multi-person. The source plans do not resolve this. Recommendation: try both during M1 benchmarking (backlog item 1.2).\n+\n+### Blender version target\n+No Blender version is specified in any source plan. Add-on API compatibility (e.g., `bpy.types.Panel` changes between 3.x and 4.x) is a decision that must be made.\n+\n+### Hardware requirements\n+No GPU/CPU requirements are defined. GPU inference needs CUDA-capable hardware; CPU-only targets need RTMPose quantization strategy.\n+\n+### Distribution model\n+Open-source marketplace add-on vs. paid release is undefined. No source plan addresses this.\n+\n+### SMPL licensing path\n+WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration. It is unclear whether a legal/compliance path exists. If blocked, WHAM should be replaced with an alternative (e.g., VideoPose3D).\n",

+    "file": ".pm/PROJECT_BRIEF.md",
+    "patch": "Index: .pm/PROJECT_BRIEF.md\n===================================================================\n--- .pm/PROJECT_BRIEF.md\t\n+++ .pm/PROJECT_BRIEF.md\t\n@@ -1,16 +1,85 @@\n-# Project Brief\r\n-\r\n-Goal: Build a Blender add-on that uses modern motion tracking / pose estimation code to convert video into usable Blender animation data.\r\n-\r\n-Initial technical direction:\r\n-- Use MMPose / RTMPose as the first backend.\r\n-- Run inference outside Blender.\r\n-- Cache results as JSON.\r\n-- Import tracked keypoints into Blender as empties, curves, or armature controls.\r\n-- Avoid embedding PyTorch directly into Blender for v1.\r\n-\r\n-Constraints:\r\n-- Work in small, reviewable tasks.\r\n-- Every task must include tests or a manual validation step.\r\n-- Do not make broad refactors unless the task explicitly requests them.\r\n-- Prefer simple, inspectable code over clever automation.\n\\ No newline at end of file\n+# Project Brief — Blender Motion Tracking Enhancement\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Purpose\n+\n+Integrate state-of-the-art human pose tracking into Blender's Video Editor for automatic camera rigging, motion retargeting, and animation. The system takes video input, produces 2D pose tracks with persistent IDs, maps them to Blender empties or armature bones, and optionally lifts to 3D.\n+\n+## Planning Sources\n+\n+The project scope is defined by three planning documents:\n+\n+- **`.pm/PLAN_SUMMARY.md`** — Technical planning summary derived from the master plan and deep research report.\n+- **`documentation/PLAN.md`** — 18-week phased implementation plan with milestones and phases.\n+- **`deep-research-report.md`** — Comparative analysis of candidate tracking backends (MMPose, SAM 2, ByteTrack, LoRATv2, WHAM).\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Recommended Architecture\n+\n+```\n+Video / Still Images\n+    → Blender Add-on Panel (launch MMPose worker, configure options)\n+        → MMPose Worker (external Python subprocess, RTMPose inference)\n+            → 2D Keypoints + Track IDs (cached JSON)\n+                → Temporal Smoothing + Gap Fill\n+                    → Blender Empties / Armature Bones\n+                        → Optional 3D Pose Lift (WHAM, phase-dependent)\n+                            → Animation Curves in Scene\n+```\n+\n+## Primary Backend: MMPose / RTMPose\n+\n+MMPose with RTMPose is the recommended v1 backend. It produces 2D keypoints directly mappable to Blender bones and empties, with real-time performance (90+ FPS on CPU, 430+ FPS on GPU) and an Apache-2.0 license.\n+\n+## Target Phases\n+\n+1. **MMPose Integration** (Weeks 1–4): Video → MMPose → empties with keypoints + track IDs.\n+2. **Armature Retargeting** (Weeks 5–8): Skeleton bone mapping, automatic armature generation, animation curves.\n+3. **Multi-Person + Object Tracking** (Weeks 9–12): SAM 2, ByteTrack, RTMO integration.\n+4. **3D Pose Lifting** (Weeks 13–15): Optional 2D→3D lift via WHAM.\n+5. **Optimization & Polish** (Weeks 16–18): Latency optimization, TensorRT, UI polish, documentation.\n+\n+## Why Heavy ML Inference Runs Outside Blender (v1)\n+\n+Blender ships its own bundled Python distribution. Embedding PyTorch and CUDA inside Blender's Python environment introduces significant complexity:\n+\n+- **Dependency conflicts:** Blender's Python has its own version and bundled packages. Adding PyTorch (1200+ MB) and CUDA toolkits risks DLL conflicts.\n+- **Stability:** A crash in the ML worker would take Blender down with it if embedded. Out-of-process keeps Blender stable.\n+- **Distribution:** Shipping a combined Blender + PyTorch installer is impractical — PyTorch alone is 1.2+ GB with CUDA dependencies.\n+- **Flexibility:** A separate worker lets users upgrade PyTorch independently, supports GPU/CPU toggle, and enables headless operation on a remote machine.\n+\n+The out-of-process design is mandated by all three planning sources.\n+\n+## Why Blender Consumes Cached Tracking Outputs\n+\n+Communication between Blender and the MMPose worker uses cached JSON files — not in-memory pipes or embedded libraries — because:\n+\n+- **Inspection & debugging:** JSON files are human-readable. Users can inspect tracking results, compare frames, and debug ID switches without rerunning inference.\n+- **Idempotency:** Tracking outputs can be cached and reused. Users can tweak visualization, retargeting, or smoothing without re-tracking video.\n+- **Decoupling:** The worker and Blender can run independently. The worker can process multiple videos; Blender can import any cached result at any time.\n+- **Simplicity:** File-based exchange avoids complex IPC protocols, shared memory, or network sockets.\n+\n+## Key Constraints\n+\n+1. **Not a Python project** — deliverable is a Blender add-on, not a standalone Python repo.\n+2. **Monocular 3D ambiguity** — 3D pose lifting is optional; depth recovery from a single camera is inherently ambiguous.\n+3. **Identity consistency** — crowded scenes require robust MOT (phase M6) to prevent ID swaps.\n+4. **17-joint limitation** — COCO keypoints don't cover spine/neck/jaw/fingers; interpolation is required for full rigs.\n+5. **SMPL licensing** — WHAM requires SMPL/SMPLify registration, which is a compliance blocker for Phase 4.\n+\n+## Scope Boundaries (Out of Scope)\n+\n+- Writing production code (planning only).\n+- Creating Blender files (.blend).\n+- Installing ML libraries or setting up environments.\n+- 3D character generation, facial expression tracking, hand pose tracking, or live camera capture (future extensions).\n+\n+## Blockers for Execution\n+\n+1. **Blender version target** — undefined; add-on API compatibility varies across 3.x/4.x.\n+2. **Hardware requirements** — no GPU/CPU specification defined.\n+3. **Distribution model** — open-source vs. paid release is undecided.\n+4. **RTMPose-m vs. RTMO** — not resolved for v1 primary model selection.\n+5. **SMPL licensing path** — WHAM integration depends on legal/compliance clearance.\n",
